antipsychotic drugs, such as haloperidol, olanzapine and aripiprazol, have different and specific effects on the expression and distribution of the neuregulin 1 and Erb B4 proteins in the brain of rats.
the expression of neuropeptide NRG1-ErBB4 signalling system in the brain is affected by short- and long term antipsychotic drug treatment.
the time-dependent effects of antipsyhotics on the expression of the NRG1-ErB4 signalling pathway may be related to their efficacy to treat schizophrenia.

the molecular mechanisms of antipsychotic action.
the role of NRG1-ErB4 signalling in antipsychotic action.
the molecular basis of the therapeutic effects of antipsycotics.

short-term treatment with haloperidol or olanzapine increased NRG1 and/or ErbB4 expression in the hippocampal region, while long-term treatment with aripiprazol or olanzopine down-regulated the expression of these proteins in the prefront cortex.
the effects of the antipsychotics are not consistent with the effects of antipsychoctic treatment on NRG1 and/or ErbB4 expression in the brain.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of NGR1 isoforms and its receptors are differentially regulated by the antipsychotic drugs, and the effect is region-specific.
antipsychotic drugs can have different effects on NRG1 and/or ErbB4 expression in the rat brain, depending on the duration of treatment, the type of antipsychotic, and the brain region.
the NRG1/ErbB4 signalling system may represent a promising therapeutic target for the treatment of schizophrenia.

the effects of antipschotics on the NRG1-ErhB4 system are time dependent and region specific.
